items.text: Heat index below 91 F (about 33 C): lower (caution) risk. Provide drinking water, plan ahead for hotter times, use sun protection.
Heat index 91-103 F (about 33-39 C): moderate risk. Remind workers to drink water often, schedule frequent breaks in a cool shaded area, use a buddy system, acclimatize workers.
Heat index 103-115 F (about 39-46 C): high risk. Schedule activities when the heat index is lower, establish and enforce work/rest schedules, limit physical exertion, watch workers closely.

Heat index above 115 F (about 46 C): very high to extreme risk. Reschedule non-essential activity; move essential tasks to the coolest part of the shift; strenuous work should not be done at or above 115 F.
Workers doing strenuous activity, wearing heavy clothing or working in direct sun need additional precautions at every risk level.
Provide adequate drinking water in convenient, visible locations close to the work area.
At moderate risk and above, drink water often: about 4 cups (about 1 litre) per hour, which is about one glass every 15 minutes.
Schedule frequent breaks in a cool, shaded area.
Set up a buddy system so workers watch each other for signs of heat-related illness.
New and returning workers doing strenuous work may be at high risk even when the heat index is low; build up their workload gradually.
At high risk and above, develop and enforce work/rest schedules and adjust work: reschedule, pace or rotate jobs, use cooling techniques.
Heat stroke signs: confusion or slurred speech, loss of consciousness, hot dry skin or profuse sweating, seizures, very high body temperature. It can be fatal if treatment is delayed.
Heat stroke first aid: call emergency medical care, stay with the worker, move them to a cool shaded area, remove outer clothing, cool them quickly with water, wet cloths and moving air.
Heat exhaustion signs: headache, nausea, dizziness, weakness, irritability, thirst, heavy sweating, raised body temperature, less urine.
Heat exhaustion first aid: move out of the heat, give liquids, remove unnecessary clothing, cool the head, face and neck, and get a medical evaluation.
Heat syncope (short fainting or dizziness after standing): sit or lie down in a cool place and slowly drink water.
Heat cramps: drink water and have a snack or electrolyte drink every 15 to 20 minutes. Avoid salt tablets.
Rhabdomyolysis signs: muscle cramps or pain, dark (tea or cola coloured) urine, weakness. Stop activity, drink water and seek immediate care.
In Tamil Nadu dial 108 for an emergency ambulance. Builders outside Tamil Nadu: check your own state's number and change NUMBER and TEXT in agent/safety.py.
